questions.q: How do the three capstone projects in this chapter relate to each other?
options: They must all be built at the same time
They're three independent options and you only build one of them
Project 2 and Project 3 are optional bonus content with no defined order
They're sequential, not parallel — Project 1 (retail analytics), then Project 2 (warehouse migration), then Project 3 (fraud detector)
questions.explain: Project 1 covers Lessons 64-69, Project 2 Lessons 70-74, and Project 3 Lessons 75-78, in that order.

questions.q: What shape does every capstone project in this chapter follow?
options: Kickoff (system-design scoping) -> build lessons layer by layer -> hardening -> wrap-up retrospective
Only a kickoff lesson — the rest is left as unguided practice
A single lesson covering the entire build with no separate phases
Wrap-up first, then build, then kickoff
questions.explain: The kickoff applies Chapter 1's system-design process; the build lessons go layer by layer; hardening and a retrospective wrap-up close it out.

questions.q: Why does this chapter insist on naming specific prior lessons for each build decision?
options: It's a formatting requirement with no bearing on understanding
Named citations are only needed for Project 3, not Projects 1 or 2
Because a project you can't explain using specific, named techniques is one you copied steps for, not one you understood
Because the grading system checks for exact lesson numbers
questions.explain: The citations mirror what Lesson 24's whiteboarding practice trains: defending a decision using specific vocabulary, not vague description.

questions.q: What does "portfolio-quality" mean for these three capstone projects?
options: Having the most lines of code possible
Being built entirely without referencing any prior course material
Built to be described out loud in a real interview, including an honest retrospective, not just finished and shipped
Passing an automated grading script with no human review
questions.explain: None of the three projects are graded pass/fail — the retrospective in each wrap-up lesson matters as much as the build itself.

questions.q: Why does Project 1 get a full five-lesson treatment while Projects 2 and 3 compress the build lessons?
options: Project 1 is more important than the other two projects
Project 1 is your first full pass through the kickoff-build-wrap-up loop, so it gets the complete treatment; later projects keep the same bookends but move faster through the middle
Projects 2 and 3 don't require a kickoff or wrap-up at all
The five-lesson format was arbitrary and has no relationship to being the first project
questions.explain: Project 2 and Project 3 compress the build lessons but keep the same kickoff-then-retrospective bookends, since that habit is what's being trained.
